backup.title: Backup
backup.intro: Creates a consistent snapshot of the application database (accounts, libraries, metadata, listening progress, bookmarks, saved lists) while the server keeps running, with its two-factor key beside it. Media files are never modified. A minimal backup adds the pictures a rescan could not put back — covers you uploaded or fetched, author portraits, category tiles; a full one adds the whole thumbnail store, rendered previews included; a quick copy is the database file alone.
backup.pathTitle: Where the server writes backups. In Docker this is a path inside the container — it sits under the folder you mapped to /config.
backup.createFullTitle: Database, two-factor key and every cover image, as one .zip
backup.createMinimalTitle: Database, two-factor key and the pictures a rescan could not put back
backup.createDatabaseTitle: A plain copy of the database file, in seconds — no zip, no key
backup.uploadBackupTitle: Upload a backup file from your computer
backup.unableToLoadSchedule: Unable to load the backup schedule
backup.restoredNotice: Restore staged from {{name}}. Restart the server to apply it.
backup.restoredNoticeDbOnly: Restore staged from {{name}}, database only — cover art left as it is. Restart the server to apply it.
backup.uploaded: Uploaded {{name}}. It's ready to restore from the list below.
backup.scheduleIntro: Each kind is a scheduled job of its own, with the same cadence, day and time choices as any other; a change here is saved at once.
backup.scheduleFullHint: Database, two-factor key and every cover image, rendered previews and face crops included — a restore needs no re-render.
backup.scheduleMinimalHint: Database, two-factor key and the pictures a rescan could not put back: covers you uploaded or fetched, series covers, author portraits, category tiles, family-tree portraits.
backup.keepAriaFull: How many full backups to keep
backup.keepAriaMinimal: How many minimal backups to keep
backup.noThumbnailStore: No thumbnail store yet — set one under
backup.retentionNote: Each kind has its own count and is pruned on its own, manual and scheduled alike: when a new one is made, older ones of that same kind beyond its number are removed. A nightly minimal backup can therefore keep a fortnight without touching the two full ones beside it. Database copies have no schedule because they are never made on a timer — you take one before trying something, and a restore leaves one behind of the database it replaced — but they pile up like anything else, so they get a count too. The automatic copies taken before an upgrade are not counted here at all: they always keep their own newest two.
backup.emptyBody: Choose "Full backup" or "Minimal backup" to make one.
backup.restoreBody: The database in {{name}} is staged and replaces the current one the next time the server starts (the current database is saved as an automatic backup first).
backup.restoreCoversNote: Cover art is put back straight away.
backup.alsoRestoreCoversHint: Off is quicker and leaves the covers you have now alone — the database comes back either way.
backup.restoreRestartWarning: You must restart the server to finish — changes made since this backup will be lost.
backup.uploadModalBody: Add a backup from your computer — a .zip (full or minimal) or a database-only .sqlite. It joins the list below, ready to restore.

containerBackup.title: Containers
containerBackup.intro: Each container's database, backed up and restored apart from Home and from the others. Video files and other media are never included. Restoring takes effect at once, with no restart.
containerBackup.backUpFailed: Unable to back up this container
containerBackup.uploadBody: A .sqlite file downloaded from this card. It joins the list, ready to restore, and is checked when you restore it.
containerBackup.notSetUpBody: Backups already taken can still be downloaded.
containerBackup.tooOldBody: This version of {{app}} can be backed up but cannot restore a backup yet. Update the container, and Restore becomes available.
containerBackup.noAnswerBody: Restoring needs the container running. Backups already taken can still be downloaded.
containerBackup.includeLabel: Include in Full and Minimal backups
containerBackup.empty: No backups of this container yet.
containerBackup.restoreBodyGames: Matches, chat, records and scores go back to how they were then, and everything played since is lost. Home and the other containers are not affected.
containerBackup.restoreBodyVideo: Watch progress, the catalog and video settings go back to how they were then, and progress made since is lost. The video files are not touched, Home and the other containers are not affected, and libraries added since are scanned again.
containerBackup.restoreBodyOther: This container's data goes back to how it was then, and changes made since are lost. Home and the other containers are not affected.
containerBackup.restoreKept: What is there now is kept on the container, so this can be undone until the next restore. A backup from a newer version of the container is refused.
containerBackup.restored: {{app}} is back to how it was on {{date}}.
containerBackup.undoNote: Restored on {{date}}. The data it replaced is kept.
containerBackup.undoBody: The data replaced on {{date}} comes back, and anything changed since then is lost. This can be done once.
containerBackup.undone: {{app}} is back to how it was before the restore.
containerBackup.deleteBody: This backup of {{app}} ({{size}}) is removed for good. {{app}} itself and its copies inside full and minimal backups are not affected.

categories.description: Shelves books land on automatically, based on their tags.
categories.rematchTitle: Recompute every book's category from its tags using the current mappings
categories.helpTagsSourceBody: When books are scanned, their genre values are saved as tags, such as detective, sci-fi, memoir, or history.
categories.helpMappingsBody: Each category has keywords. If a book tag contains one of those keywords, the book can be placed in that category.
categories.helpPriorityBody: If multiple keywords match the same book, the keyword with the higher priority wins.
categories.helpFallbackTitle: No match goes to General / Other
categories.helpFallbackBody: Books without a matching keyword stay in General / Other until a better keyword is added.
categories.helpExampleBody: A book has the tag historical mystery. If Mystery & Thriller has keyword mystery with priority 20, and History has keyword history with priority 10, the book goes to Mystery & Thriller because mystery matches and has the higher priority.
categories.helpNote: Open a category and use <bold>Mappings</bold> to add keywords manually, or <bold>Tags</bold> to turn a scanned tag into a keyword. After changing mappings, run <bold>Re-match all</bold> to update existing books.
categories.unableToLoadMappings: Unable to reload the keyword mappings
categories.unableToAddTagAsKeyword: Unable to add tag as keyword
categories.name: Name
categories.deleteMovesBooks_one: Its {{count}} book moves to General / Other.
categories.deleteMovesBooks_other: Its {{count}} books move to General / Other.
categories.deleteNoBooks: No books are in this category.
categories.deleteWhatSurvives: Its keyword mappings are deleted with it; the books themselves and their files are not touched.
categories.noTagsYet: No tags yet. Scan a library and tags appear from book genres.

video.deleteBody2: Your video files are not touched. Add the library again and the video app scans the same folder afresh.

video.editKindMovies: A library of films. What a library holds is set when it is made; for TV shows, make a library of its own.
video.folderChangeHint: The video app scans the new folder when you save. Titles found there again keep their posters and everyone's watch progress; titles no longer there leave the library.
video.languageHint: The language titles, descriptions and episode names are fetched from TMDB in. Changing it fetches them again.

libraries.rescanIntro: Re-index this library from disk. Your files are never modified, and manually edited metadata is kept.
libraries.rescanScopeNote: These choices apply to this scan only — edit the library to change its defaults.
libraries.deleteBody1: This will remove the library and all its book records, metadata, series, and genres from the database.
libraries.deleteBody2: Your files on disk will not be touched. You can re-add this library at any time and it will be re-scanned from the same folder.
libraries.takeOwnershipBody1: This will give you manager access so you can manage this private library. The action is logged for audit history.
libraries.takeOwnershipBody2: The library contents and existing owner are not deleted. Files on disk are not changed.

phoneBackups.intro: Phones ticked here don't send photos that are already in this library — the photos you backed up some other way before (Immich, say). A photo already here is recorded as backed up, and nothing is stored twice. New photos go to the member's personal library as usual.
phoneBackups.cannotOpen: {{member}} can't open this library, so this link doesn't count. Give them access, or untick it.
phoneBackups.none: No phone can be linked yet: none of the members who can open this library has set up a phone for backup.
phoneBackups.syncOffBody: Phones can be linked now; they back up once phone-backup networks are listed.
phoneBackups.howBody: A link counts from then on: photos a phone already stored in its personal library stay there. A photo deleted from this library after the phone has sent it is not sent again. Stop the old backup app on the phone, or new photos arrive twice.

libraries.noChildFolders: No child folders found. The current folder can still be used.

libraries.scanSourcesHint: Select items to scan. Drag the handle or use the arrows to change the order in which they are processed.

backSides.title: Back sides
backSides.hint: A print scanned on both sides stays one photo: the back is kept with the front and shown with Flip, not catalogued as a photo of its own. Files are paired by name, in the order below.
backSides.epsonDesc: {name}_b is the back. When the enhanced copy {name}_a is kept instead of the original, the back follows it.
backSides.customDesc: {name} stands for the front's file name; everything else is matched as written, ignoring case.
backSides.keepNote: Pairs already recorded stay paired if you turn this off. A back added from a photo is named with the first pattern: {{pattern}}.
backSides.checkHint: Counts, from file names alone, what a rescan would pair. Nothing changes until you save and rescan.
backSides.checkTitle_one: {{count}} back would pair on the next rescan
backSides.checkTitle_other: {{count}} backs would pair on the next rescan
backSides.checkMatched_one: {{count}} file fits a pattern and has a front beside it
backSides.checkMatched_other: {{count}} files fit a pattern and have a front beside them
backSides.checkRetire_one: {{count}} of them is catalogued as a photo today and would leave the grid, keeping everything it carries. Split off the back brings it back.
backSides.checkRetire_other: {{count}} of them are catalogued as photos today and would leave the grid, keeping everything they carry. Split off the back brings any of them back.
backSides.checkUnmatched_one: {{count}} file fits a pattern but has no front — it stays an ordinary photo
backSides.checkUnmatched_other: {{count}} files fit a pattern but have no front — they stay ordinary photos

libraries.tagEncodingHint: Repairs garbled tag text (e.g. "Ðàíåå" → "Ранее") for files whose tags were saved in this legacy encoding. Correctly stored tags are left untouched.
libraries.uploadStandardHint: Up to 10 GB per file — big enough for any single upload, small enough that a runaway upload can't fill the disk.
libraries.uploadCustomHint: Set a maximum size for each file.
libraries.externalReadOnlyHint: External libraries are read-only — uploads are disabled.
libraries.modeManagedFull: Managed — this app owns the files
libraries.modeExternalFull: External — read-only, managed outside this app

libraryMembers.publicContributor: Everyone can view, download, and add content.

libraryMembers.noMembersYet: No individual users or groups added yet.

logs.description: Review activity history and clean up old records.
logs.searchAria: Search logs by detail, event, user or IP
logs.emptyFiltered: No log entries match — widen the window or clear a filter.
logs.deleteOldBody: Log entries older than this are permanently deleted. Nothing else is touched, and the entries currently on screen stay unless they fall outside the window.
logs.appDescription: What {{app}} recorded — its events, or the newest lines of its server log — read from it through the gateway. Nothing is kept here.
logs.sourceUnavailableBody: Its logs are read from the container itself, so they show while it answers. The Dashboard says how it stands; Infrastructure › Services tests the connection.

genres.description: The genres your family browses films and shows by. Films arrive with genres from their .nfo files and from TMDB, often in two languages and several spellings; this list decides what each of those becomes.
genres.unavailableBody: Genres are kept by the video engine, so this page needs it running.
genres.name: Name
genres.empty: No genres yet. Until there are, films and shows keep the genres their .nfo files and TMDB gave them.
genres.seedBody: Adds TMDB's film and TV genres, with the other language's names and common spellings as keywords. TMDB's double TV genres ("Sci-Fi & Fantasy") lead to both of theirs, and "TV Movie" is hidden.
genres.unsortedTitle: Found genres not in your list
genres.unsortedBody: Films still show these as they came. Add each to one of your genres, make it a genre of its own, or hide it.
genres.unsortedNone: Every genre your films have is in your list or hidden.
genres.hiddenBody: Films that have these don't show them. Nothing is removed from your files; × shows one again, and it goes back to Found genres not in your list.
genres.keywordsTitle: Keywords: other names for this genre
genres.keywordsHint: A film that arrives with any of these genres from its files or TMDB gets this genre instead. One keyword can belong to several genres.
genres.mergeConfirmBody: Its titles and keywords move to "{{into}}", and "{{name}}" becomes one of its keywords. The files are not touched.
genres.deleteBody_one: {{count}} title loses this genre. Its name and keywords become hidden genres, so they don't come back on their own. The files are not touched.
genres.deleteBody_other: {{count}} titles lose this genre. Its name and keywords become hidden genres, so they don't come back on their own. The files are not touched.
genres.helpIntro: Every genre a film arrives with ends up one of four ways:
genres.helpKeywordTitle: A keyword of one of your genres
genres.helpKeywordBody: "Comedy" is a keyword of Комедия, so films show Комедия. A keyword can lead to two genres: "Sci-Fi & Fantasy" to both Фантастика and Фэнтези.
genres.helpNameTitle: The name of one of your genres
genres.helpNameBody: "Драма" is in your list, so films show Драма, whatever its case or spelling of ё.
genres.helpFoundBody: "Biography" leads nowhere yet, so films show Biography as it came. It waits under Found genres not in your list until you decide.
genres.helpHiddenBody: "TV Movie" is hidden, so films don't show it, in the filters or on the TV either.
genres.helpNote: Nothing here changes your files: the genres they carry are only read. Changes show at once everywhere, with no rescan.

organization.sharedNote: Tags and book categories are shared: a change applies everywhere they are used, whichever application you opened them from.
organization.categoriesBody: The shelves books are sorted onto, by keyword rules.
organization.tagsBody: Free labels, from scanned genres or added by hand.
organization.tagsAppliesTo: Books · Gallery photos · Albums · Slideshows · Stories · Family-tree people
organization.genresBody: Genres for films and shows, mapped from their files and TMDB.
organization.genresAppliesTo: Movies · TV shows in Video libraries
organization.videoNotSetUp: Video isn't connected to this server.
organization.videoDown: The video engine isn't answering, so genres can't be edited until it is back.
organization.appDescription: Organization and cleanup tools for {{app}}. Shared ones open the one editor every application uses.
organization.duplicatesBody: Find the same photo kept twice and choose which copy stays.
organization.missingBody: Photos whose files are no longer on disk.
